clue.text: Uncomplicated type, not altogether sensible, shoots back

indicators.note: not altogether means the word sensible loses a piece, here its final letter
back tells us the word for shoots is written in the opposite direction

blocks.note: sensible means sane, of sound mind
shoots a gun, fires it

explanation.surface: A sensible-ish person firing off simple-typed messages in return.
explanation.walkthrough: Type here is typography, not a kind of person; the answer is two words run together in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A sans serif font lacks the small decorative strokes at letter ends, so it is a plain, simple style of print.

clue.text: Jack counts up – he quickly passes 5

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for counts is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: jack and AB are both words for a sailor
counts on someone, relies on them

explanation.surface: A sailor tallying something before quickly overtaking another.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 is the answer to 5 down, FROM TOP TO BOTTOM: an abseiler descends a rope fast, passing a cliff from top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone descending a rock face on a rope travels rapidly downward, covering its whole height.

clue.text: Serve in revised matins in elevated religious state

indicators.note: something revised has been reworked, so the letters of matins are rearranged
in places the word for serve inside the rearranged letters

blocks.note: to do is to serve or suffice, as in 'that will do'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Serving at a reworked morning service while in a lofty spiritual condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sainthood is the exalted status of a canonised holy person, a high spiritual rank.

clue.text: Novel instrument and music – each of them is this

blocks.note: surface reading: a new kind of instrument and its music
setter's reading: a novel, a legal instrument and written music are all things one can read

explanation.surface: An inventive new instrument with its own music, described somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like 'new', but it is a book; instrument is a legal document; music here is a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Books, legal documents and printed scores all carry text or notation that a person can make sense of by reading.

clue.text: How this solution is put into place, fully

definitions.text: How this solution is put into place

blocks.clueFragment: How this solution is put into place
blocks.note: first meaning: a down answer is written into the grid starting at the top square
second meaning: completely, throughout

explanation.walkthrough: This clue is for a down entry, so it describes its own direction of entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means thoroughly or completely, covering everything, as when a house is cleaned in every part.

clue.text: Awfully proud about grant, leading to heavy fall

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly mangled, so the letters of proud are rearranged
about means the rearranged letters wrap around the word for grant

blocks.note: taken as written
to own a fact is to grant or admit it

explanation.surface: An arrogant recipient of a grant heading for a big tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge of rain is a heavy precipitation, and rain is said to fall.

clue.text: Offering as bait from end of rod, fishing

indicators.note: end of tells us to keep only the final letter of rod

blocks.note: last letter of rod
angling is fishing with a rod and line

explanation.surface: An angler holding out bait on the line at the tip of the rod.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle something is to hold it out as a temptation, like a carrot before a donkey.

clue.text: Affected by rain around North, then South, got destroyed

indicators.note: around means the word for affected by rain encloses a compass letter

blocks.note: rained on, so wet
N is the compass abbreviation
the same word is understood a second time, this time round the next compass point
S is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A rain-soaked region, north then south, ruined by the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: WET is used twice: once around N, then again around S, giving WENT and WEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Went west is an idiom for being lost, ruined or killed.

clue.text: Recount including old clubs – transfer 5 or 14 across, say

indicators.note: including means the word for recount holds the other letters inside it

blocks.note: to recount a story is to relate it
O is a standard abbreviation for old
C is the card suit abbreviation

explanation.surface: Retelling a tale involving old golf clubs being moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 and 14 across are the themed phrases FROM TOP TO BOTTOM and FROM LEFT TO RIGHT, which describe a move from one place to another.
explanation.definitionFit: To move something from one position to another is to shift its location.

clue.text: Repetitive phrase from ghost in a tomb

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

blocks.note: hidden across ghost in a tomb

explanation.surface: A ghost in a tomb moaning the same refrain over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: In music an ostinato is a short motif persistently repeated throughout a passage.

clue.text: Outside parties held back by force in extremely dark time

indicators.note: held back means the letters for outside parties are read in the opposite direction
held by force means the word for force holds those letters within it

blocks.note: an Independent stands outside the political parties; IND is its abbreviation
might is power or force

explanation.surface: Independents kept back by force during a very dark period.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve at night is the middle of the night, when it is darkest.

clue.text: Divert wagons I had ordered westward ahead of time

indicators.note: in an across entry, westward means right to left, so the words for wagons and I had are reversed

blocks.note: carts are wagons
I'd is the contraction of I had
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A wagon train sent west early to throw pursuers off.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert someone's attention is to draw it away elsewhere.

clue.text: Like ten to four on watch? Just the reverse

definitions.text: Like ten to four on watch?

blocks.clueFragment: Like ten to four on watch?
blocks.note: first meaning: on a clock face the 10 and the 4 face each other across the dial
second meaning: the contrary

explanation.walkthrough: Ten to four reads as a time, but it means the positions 10 and 4 on a watch face, directly across from each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Positions facing each other across a circle are on contrary sides, and the contrary of something is its reverse.

clue.text: How to read how one-two generally proceeds

blocks.note: first meaning: English text is read in this direction
second meaning: a boxer's one-two is a left jab followed by a right

explanation.walkthrough: A one-two in boxing is a quick left then right punch; this is also the direction this across entry is written.
explanation.definitionFit: English is read starting at the left side of the page, and a classic one-two combination throws the left first.

clue.text: Following up legal changes, both 14 across and 5

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters of up legal are reworked

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for following
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pursuing amendments to the law, applying to two earlier clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 across and 5 down are FROM LEFT TO RIGHT and FROM TOP TO BOTTOM: something spanning a sheet both ways fills it.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert covering a sheet entirely runs across its width and down its height.

clue.text: Moron I’ve converted who’ll swallow all kinds of things?

definitions.text: who’ll swallow all kinds of things?

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gullible fool, newly converted, who will believe anything at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Swallow suggests gullibility, fitting a moron, but literally an omnivore eats every kind of food.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnivore eats both plant and animal food, so it consumes every sort of thing.

clue.text: Tissue a body needs, crying about private upset

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so private is read upward
about means the word for crying wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: a lament is a crying out in grief
a GI is a US private soldier

explanation.surface: A distressed soldier weeping, needing comfort for his body.
explanation.definitionFit: Ligaments are bands of tough fibrous tissue joining bones, which every skeleton requires.

clue.text: Eggs on a great deal, engulfing the speaker in lots of applause

indicators.note: engulfing means the phrase for a great deal swallows the word for the speaker

blocks.note: ova are eggs
tons, informally, a great deal
the speaker refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: Egging on a speaker so much that the crowd applauds heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovations are bursts of enthusiastic clapping from an audience.

clue.text: Out of bounds? Trendy form of punishment covers it

indicators.note: covers means the form of punishment wraps around the final word

blocks.note: in means fashionable
a fine is a monetary penalty
taken as written

explanation.surface: Going out of bounds earns a fashionable penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Out of bounds normally means forbidden; here it means beyond all limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something limitless has no boundary at all, so it lies beyond every bound.

clue.text: Royal title that diminishes 5

blocks.note: first meaning
second meaning: 5 is FROM TOP TO BOTTOM, and loftiness lessens as you go down

explanation.walkthrough: 5 refers to 5 down, FROM TOP TO BOTTOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal personages are styled Your Highness, and the quality of being tall naturally shrinks as you descend.

clue.text: In testing situation, misrepresented grand larceny of a kind

indicators.note: misrepresented means shown wrongly, so the letters of grand are jumbled
in places the jumbled letters inside the word for testing situation

blocks.note: a lab is where tests are carried out
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tricky courtroom where grand larceny is wrongly portrayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A land grab is a sudden seizure of territory, often illegal, so it is a type of theft.

clue.text: Excel in ring, being absurdly tough and fit

indicators.note: absurdly suggests nonsense, so the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of tough and fit, without and

explanation.surface: A boxer who dominates because he is ridiculously hard and in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The word and is a joiner here, not part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent in a boxing bout is to be the better combatant.

clue.text: Pawn opening followed by a check, pieces captured – level drawing position

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of pawn
captured means the word for pieces is held inside the word for check

blocks.note: first letter of pawn
taken as written
to vet is to check
chess pieces are men

explanation.surface: A chess game commentary: pawn opening, a check, pieces taken, a drawn position.
explanation.walkthrough: Drawing here is art, not a drawn game: pavement artists draw in chalk on the flat walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavement is a flat walkway where street artists chalk their pictures.

clue.text: Records debates and leaves – they’re all this

blocks.note: surface reading: someone writes down debates and then departs
setter's reading: vinyl records, arguments and tree leaves each have an A and B face or a for and against

explanation.surface: A clerk minuting debates before leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Records, debates and leaves look like verbs but are nouns: discs, arguments and pages each have two faces.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc has an A and B face, a debate pro and con, a page front and back.

clue.text: It’s nothing trivial, for example, backing Indian leader

indicators.note: backing means the preceding words are written in reverse order

blocks.note: O is zero
minor means unimportant
e.g. abbreviates for example

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about a trivial matter, then an Indian chief.
explanation.walkthrough: Indian here means Native American: Geronimo was an Apache leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Geronimo was a renowned Apache war chief who resisted US forces in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Widespread European employment for spa worker

blocks.note: mass as an adjective means on a large scale
E is the abbreviation for European
use is employment of something

explanation.surface: Plentiful European jobs available in health resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman giving massages is a typical member of staff at a health resort.
